Simple meaning: The main folder containing your app’s code and configuration
Why it matters to you: You must open Terminal inside this folder before running most project commands

Simple meaning: A text-based way to control your computer
Why it matters to you: On your Mac, use the Terminal app or the integrated terminal in VS Code

Simple meaning: A version-control tool that records changes to code
Why it matters to you: Lets you see what changed, save a checkpoint, and collaborate safely

Simple meaning: A project folder tracked by Git
Why it matters to you: Your app appears to be inside a Git repository

Simple meaning: A separate line of work in Git
Why it matters to you: Your output mentions a branch named feat/ux-logic-graph

Simple meaning: Git’s pointer to the currently selected saved version
Why it matters to you: Think: “where Git says I am right now”

Simple meaning: A named saved checkpoint in Git
Why it matters to you: fddbb7b is the short ID of one commit

Simple meaning: A private Python workspace for one project
Why it matters to you: It keeps this app’s Python packages separate from other apps

Simple meaning: The programming language used by your backend
Why it matters to you: Your project uses Python 3.9 in its virtual environment

Simple meaning: Folder holding Python libraries installed for the project
Why it matters to you: The long list of flask, sqlalchemy, etc. belongs here

Simple meaning: Reusable code installed into a project
Why it matters to you: Flask, SQLAlchemy, and Alembic are dependencies

Simple meaning: A Python framework for making web applications and APIs
Why it matters to you: Likely the main backend of your project

Simple meaning: A defined way for programs to communicate with each other
Why it matters to you: Example: your frontend sends a request to your Flask backend

Simple meaning: A Python tool for working with databases using Python code
Why it matters to you: It helps your app create, read, update, and delete database records

Simple meaning: Structured storage for app data, such as users, cases, or leads
Why it matters to you: Your app likely uses SQLAlchemy to connect to it

Simple meaning: A tool that tracks database structure changes
Why it matters to you: Used when you add a database column or table without losing existing data

Simple meaning: A saved instruction for changing database structure
Why it matters to you: Example: “add a phone_number column to the clients table”

Simple meaning: JSON Web Token: a signed temporary “proof of login”
Why it matters to you: Used by your app to recognize an authenticated user

Simple meaning: A production server that runs Python web apps
Why it matters to you: Usually used after deployment to a Linux server, not normally for Mac local development

Simple meaning: A macOS Finder metadata file
Why it matters to you: Usually should not be saved to Git

Simple meaning: Folder containing JavaScript packages
Why it matters to you: It usually belongs to a frontend or API subfolder, such as apps/api

Simple meaning: A file telling Git which files it must not track
Why it matters to you: .venv, node_modules, secrets, and .DS_Store should normally be ignored
